newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait undecided on Mideast economic summit.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait undecided on Mideast economic summit.

text.p: Kuwait has yet to decide whether to attend the Middle East-North Africa (MENA) economic summit in Qatar in November, a minister was quoted on Sunday as saying.
"Kuwait has not yet decided on its stand on attending the Doha economic summit," Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan told al-Rai al-Aam newspaper.
"We still do not know if the summit will convene or not," he told the Kuwaiti daily on the fringes of a two-day meeting in Qatar by Gulf Arab economy and finance ministers.

Qatar, current head of the regional Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) alliance, last week suggested that its invitation for Israel to attend the summit would depend on the resumption of stalled Middle East peace talks.

Senior Syrian officials this month toured Gulf Arab states to urge them not to hold the summit. Syria, a key Arab ally against Iraq in the 1991 Gulf War, has boycotted the annual event hosted by Egypt last year.

Diplomatic sources and regional newspapers have said that GCC members Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and United Arab Emirates, all strongly offended by Israel's building of a Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem, appeared to support the Syrian demand. Oman and Bahrain are also GCC members.
Rodhan told the newspaper that invitations to the summit had yet to be sent, stressing that the GCC talks in Doha were not aimed at discussing the fate of the summit.
But the daily quoted Gulf sources as saying the ministers discussed the possibility of the alliance's secretary-general attending the summit as a representative for all GCC states.
"The sources said that the proposal is being discussed with interest at the highest levels in each Gulf country," it added.
The conservative oil states of the GCC have lifted the secondary Arab economic boycott of Israel -- third-party firms which deal with the Jewish state -- but do not have diplomatic ties with Israel.
Only Oman and Qatar have trade links with Israel but ties have cooled in recent months.
